provenance.J_air_column: amended air objective (Amendment 4). The committed record results_e11_cross_fidelity.json holds the PRE-amendment column and rho = -0.6; the manuscript quotes the amended one. Both are on disk and the difference is the amendment, not a correction made after seeing a result.
provenance.limitation: n = 6 designs from ONE task. Every slope below has 4 degrees of freedom. rho is a RANK correlation on 6 points and takes values in multiples of 1/70; -0.7714 is 5 losses out of 15 pairs.

ranking_note: the amended J_air and T_in_max columns induce the SAME ranking on these six designs, which is why rho(J_liq,J_air) and rho(J_liq,T_in_max) agree to four decimals. That agreement is a property of six points, not two independent confirmations.

lambda_provenance_defect.effect: 133.7 was computed as 184/1.376. The slope fitted to these six designs is 1.386, not 1.376, so the ratio the fits actually give is 133.0. The 0.5% difference changes no verdict and no record: every arm, every re-scoring and every table in the campaign used 133.7 as pre-registered, and re-running at 133.0 would be re-choosing a weight after seeing the data. It is recorded because it is the same defect class as (7) and (12): a number in prose that no record produces.
lambda_provenance_defect.action: keep 133.7 as the pre-registered weight; quote 1.386 as the fitted slope; state the discrepancy wherever 133.7 is derived.

lambda_uncertainty.fieller_note: finite but a factor of 141 wide; q2 = 0.07101 is barely positive, so the interval is extremely sensitive to the denominator slope's SE
lambda_uncertainty.reading: lambda = 133.7 is a ratio of two slopes fitted to SIX designs from one task. Its own 95% interval is a factor of ~7 wide and contains both ends of the 576-pair bracket, so '133.7 lies outside both confidence intervals' is a comparison between a +-38% number and two intervals quoted to three significant figures, and must be read as a statement about the pooled fits rather than as evidence that 133.7 is wrong.
